newsitem.title: USA: Dole on California bus tour in race for key state.
newsitem.headline: Dole on California bus tour in race for key state.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole hammered away at President Bill Clinton's immigration policy on Saturday, hoping to cut his Democratic rival's commanding lead in California.
"I smell victory in California," Dole told a large crowd at a park in this fertile agricultural region of the state.

Standing in front of a huge mural emblazoned with the word "Trust", Dole criticised the president for not doing more to stop illegal immigration, a major issue in the state, and said Clinton's "war on California" hurt businesses and farmers.
Dole repeated charges that the White House was rushing through naturalisation of legal aliens so they could vote on election day "even if they had criminal records."
"That is an outrage," he said. "That is an outrage."

At a rally in Visalla, Dole repeated his list of White House ethics problems, pointing to questions about possibly illegal donations to the Democrats from foreign interests, the Whitewater affair and improper White House acquisition of FBI files on Republicans.
This huge state is the nation's biggest campaign prize, with 54 of the 270 Electoral College votes needed to win the presidency.

Dole, on a bus tour of the central part of the state, was focusing much of his time and advertising budget on California during the last 10 days of the campaign, based partly on a poll showing he had narrowed Clinton's lead.

The Dole campaign on Friday unveiled an immigration advertisement targeted at California. It includes footage of prisoners and police officers hustling someone into a squad car while the announcer complains of 20,000 illegal immigrants in prisons and 2 million statewide.
Immigration has been a hot issue in California, where voters approved by 59 percent a proposition to deny nearly all benefits to illegal immigrants. Its implementation has been held up in the courts.

Although a Los Angeles Times poll earlier this week showed Dole trailing Clinton by a 20-point margin in the state, Dole spokesman Nelson Warfield said the campaign's internal polling showed "a lot of reason for confidence in California." He did not elaborate.
Clinton has made a concentrated effort to woo California since taking office, visiting the state about 30 times and dispensing government defence contracts and other aid.
Introducing Dole, California Republican Gov. Pete Wilson called Clinton the president who "declared war on the West."
He and Dole both charged that the FBI was not doing needed background checks on applicants for citizenship and up to 10 percent of immigrants had criminal records.

The FBI has said that 10 percent of immigrants showed up on FBI files but that this did not indicate that they had criminal records. There has been an upsurge in naturalisation applications, apparently resulting partly from new laws restricting government benefits to legal aliens.
Dole, who has lashed out at reporters in recent days accusing them of ignoring White House ethics problems, said on Saturday he was sorry if he had offended the press corps.
He then repeated his charges that the press was not going after Clinton on ethics.
